sections.skill: Write an image request with subject, setting, style and composition

questions.prompt: What does an image generator do?

choices.text: Searches the internet and returns an existing photo that matches the words you typed
Turns a text description into a picture

questions.correct_answer: Turns a text description into a picture
questions.intro: An IMAGE GENERATOR turns a text description into a picture. A vague request ("a dog") gets a random result; a useful one names four things. SUBJECT: what is shown ("a brown puppy holding a red ball"). SETTING: where and when ("in a snowy backyard at sunset"). STYLE: how it looks ("watercolor," "flat cartoon," "photo-like"). COMPOSITION: how it is framed ("close-up," "wide view," "puppy on the left, empty space on the right for a title"). Add the PURPOSE and shape ("square poster for a school bake sale") so the result fits where it will be used. Leave out details that do not matter.

sections.skill: Compare an image request with ordering a custom cake

questions.prompt: "A soccer ball" on the cake is like which part of an image request?
questions.intro: When you order a custom cake, you tell the baker WHAT is on it (a soccer ball), the THEME or setting (green field), the LOOK (bright and simple, not realistic), and the LAYOUT (ball in the middle, "Happy 10th, Sam" along the bottom). You also say the size and occasion. If you only say "a cake," you get whatever the baker imagines. An image request works the same way: subject, setting, style and composition.

sections.title: Apply it

sections.skill: Avoid conflicting, ambiguous and unfair image requests

questions.prompt: "A minimalist poster packed with decorations" has what problem?
questions.intro: Image requests have their own traps. Too many details can conflict ("minimalist" plus "packed with decorations"). Words with two meanings confuse tools ("a bat" could be an animal or sports gear). Asking for a living artist's name as a style raises fairness and rights questions, so describe the qualities you want instead ("bold outlines, bright flat colors"). And never make realistic images of real people doing things they did not do without their consent, or pass them off as real.

questions.prompt: "A bat on a table" could confuse a tool. Why?
